topics.label: Course Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing for the lecture, outlining the course structure, lecturer background, and key learning goals.

topics.label: Biological Origins of Cancer and Sources of DNA Mutations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish cancer as a micro-evolutionary genetic disease and outline the intrinsic and extrinsic processes driving the accumulation of mutations.

topics.label: Environmental Exposures, Public Perception, and Geographic Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine common environmental carcinogen exposures, public debates regarding cancer causation, and epidemiological evidence demonstrating geographical variations in cancer incidence.

topics.label: Infectious Agents and Pathogen-Driven Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail how biological pathogens drive cancer development, focusing on the epidemiological and molecular mechanisms of Epstein-Barr virus in Burkitt lymphoma.

topics.label: Mechanisms of Mutagenesis by Chemical and Physical Agents
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore how dietary toxins, radiation, and chemical carcinogens undergo metabolic activation to induce DNA adducts and mutations.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Multi-Stage Carcinogenesis, and Host Susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the distinction between cancer initiators and promoters, the role of chronic inflammation, and how host developmental stages affect cancer vulnerability.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro techniques used to establish whether substances are carcinogenic and evaluate overall risk.
